assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ab initio molecular dynamics put electronic structure and atomic motion in one scheme, making simulation of liquids, interfaces and reactions in condensed phase routine. It is a true game-changer in my own field and has shaped chemistry, materials and biomolecular simulation for four decades, with direct quantitative links to experiment.
assessment.attribution: Car and Parrinello's 1985 paper is the unambiguous origin; the two-person configuration is clean and fits the three-laureate limit with room to spare.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by decades of independent use and countless codes; recognition is arguably overdue, with no stability concerns about the method itself.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers to treat it as chemistry or as physics/materials methodology.
DFT and simulation methods were recognised in 1998 and 2013, which could be read as partial coverage of the area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair to another without double-strand cleavage by pairing deaminase chemistry with a programmable DNA-binding protein. It is a completely new capability with clinical consequences already visible, and the chemistry of the nucleobase conversions is central.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual driver; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees on the cytosine and adenine base editors. A Liu-alone or Liu plus a second name configuration is plausible, and I choose the names most tied to the primary inventions.
assessment.maturity: Rapid replication, many therapeutic programmes and first clinical results; recognition is timely though the CRISPR prize in 2020 sets a close precedent.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee wishes to follow the 2020 CRISPR prize so soon.
Allocation among Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, and the role of independent Japanese work (Nishida, Kondo) on cytidine deamination editing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframed drug discovery by using small molecules to recruit E3 ligases and destroy, not inhibit, proteins. It has already had clear consequences: degraders are in clinical trials and the mechanism of thalidomide-type drugs was clarified.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept and its chemistry, with Ciulli providing structure-guided design and VHL ligand work. The molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito and others) has a separate credit story that cannot fit into three names.
assessment.maturity: Strong mechanistic confirmation across many labs; clinical efficacy is still being established, so late-stage outcomes are not yet in hand.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with PROTAC and molecular-glue parts needing different recognition.
Clinical validation is incomplete; the thalidomide/cereblon credit (Handa, Ito) is difficult to place.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dye-sensitized mesoscopic solar cells showed that molecular photochemistry on nanocrystalline oxide could convert sunlight efficiently, opening a whole line of molecular photovoltaics. The idea was original and simple and has had a lasting consequence for energy chemistry.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel paper is the decisive contribution; Grätzel is the dominant figure, so a one- or two-name prize is straightforward. Hagfeldt is an important developer but later.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of confirmation, though commercial impact has been modest; its descendants (perovskites) show the scientific influence.
uncertainties: Limited commercial penetration may weigh against the 'game-changer' standard.
Whether O'Regan, as a postdoc, should share credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule clusters made genome sequencing cheap and ubiquitous. The consequences for biology and medicine have been enormous and the underlying chemistry is genuinely molecular.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived the Solexa chemistry; other credited names (Rothberg, Mayer, Ju) represent parallel platforms. A two-person prize around the Solexa/Illumina chemistry is cleanest but would have to neglect competing technologies.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and globally adopted; recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Credit is split across competing platforms and companies.
Sequencing prizes were awarded earlier (1980); whether this extends it enough.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a workhorse in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, giving general access to aryl amines. The impact is vast and daily, although it extends a field already recognised in 2010.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic version independently and in parallel; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work was a precursor. Two names fit well.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely used, no stability concerns about the science.
uncertainties: Weight to give Kosugi/Migita precursor work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers rose in efficiency within a decade from a few percent to over 25 percent and spawned a broad materials field. It is a clear, fast game-changer in photovoltaics and optoelectronics.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitised cell; Park and Snaith made the key solid-state advances. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel are also major contributors, so a three-name limit leaves out significant credit.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is independently confirmed, but long-term stability and manufacturing are unresolved, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Device stability and toxicity issues remain.
Contested credit among many leading groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy-landscape theory with the funnel concept explained how proteins fold quickly and reliably, and was linked to experiment through kinetics and phi-value analysis. It is conceptually simple and has shaped how chemists think about folding, binding and function.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are theory leaders with Bryngelson; Fersht provided the quantitative experimental mapping. Dill is also prominent, so the three-person limit forces choices.
assessment.maturity: Conceptually mature, with decades of testing, although AlphaFold and the 2024 prize may have reduced the sense of urgency.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 protein structure prediction prize.
Priority among Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson and Dill.
